product_target.statement: Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate consumed through public crate interfaces by games and by a minimal validation executable; this repository delivers the substrate and a non-game public-API validation harness, not any particular game and not the later Product One explorer demo.

documents.rationale: States the current product identity (reusable Rust voxel-world substrate), repository deliverables, public boundary, correctness and validation commitments, and non-goals. Explicitly demotes the embedded Product One explorer prose to later-consumer vision that does not authorize game deliverables in Moria. Root README points to this document as the product definition.

Self-describes as support for the Moria program brief and states it does not add deliverables. Enumerates public surface characteristics (identity, queries, mutations, streaming, persistence, registered objects, diagnostics) without claiming a different product target or expanding scope.

Repository orientation that points at the program brief as the product definition and labels the interface note as non-scoping support. README assertions about which seed is binding are navigational evidence, not an independent product-boundary instrument.

claims.statement: Moria is the reusable voxel-world substrate defined by docs/seeds/mixed-project-brief.md.
The brief deliberately includes a small later-product vision inside an otherwise binding current-product document.
Only the current substrate commitments are deliverables in this repository.
docs/seeds/substrate-interface-reference.md supplies supporting technical context without expanding product scope.
Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate. It is consumed through public crate interfaces by games and by a minimal validation executable.
This repository delivers the substrate, not any particular game.

The current product owns deterministic seed-based generation, sparse voxel storage, bounded streaming, mutation, surface extraction, persistence, and read-only diagnostics. These capabilities must remain useful to multiple downstream consumers.
Generation is deterministic for the same versioned parameters and seed.

External consumers can create and identify a world, request bounded regions, observe readiness, query material truth, submit bounded edits, and persist deltas. A consumer must not reach into storage, meshing, or scheduler internals.

The validation executable uses exactly these public interfaces. It may provide a free-fly camera and diagnostics sufficient to exercise the crate, but it is not a game prototype and owns no privileged world path.

Generation is deterministic for the same versioned parameters and seed. Mutation is admitted through a bounded command API and committed atomically. Persistence restores the same authoritative material state. Derived meshes and diagnostics never become authoritative world state.

Streaming must bound resident work and expose observable lifecycle states. Background results carry generation identities so stale work cannot replace newer truth. Failures remain typed and observable to public consumers.

Headless fixtures cover generation, query, mutation, persistence, and lifecycle behavior. A small visual fixture demonstrates that a relocated external consumer can render and edit through the public API. Performance is reported with machine identity; this brief does not establish a machine-specific correctness threshold.

Moria does not implement game rules, combat, inventory, AI, narrative systems, characters, animation, authored levels, or production content. References to possible consumers explain interface pressure only.
After the reusable substrate ships, a separate Product One repository may place a third-person explorer in a generated region with hills, a dense mixed forest, a river, and a cave.
After the reusable substrate ships, a separate Product One repository may place a third-person explorer in a generated region with hills, a dense mixed forest, a river, and a cave.
That later game-facing demo may use skeletal animation and a curated cliff-to-cave traversal to communicate the world.

Those later paragraphs are future-consumer context embedded in this binding program brief. They do not authorize a player controller, character mesh, animation clips, forest population workload, curated route, or game asset in Moria.
This reference supports the Moria program brief. It describes the reusable surface that downstream consumers need and does not add deliverables.
It describes the reusable surface that downstream consumers need and does not add deliverables.
World identity combines format version, generation parameters, and seed.
Queries return readiness and bounded authoritative material observations.
Mutations are commands with explicit bounds, admission failures, and commit revisions.
Streaming exposes requested, loading, resident, evicted, and failed states.
Persistence records authoritative deltas rather than derived meshes.
Registered objects can participate in queries without becoming game entities.
Diagnostics report lifecycle and bounded work without exposing mutable internal handles.

deferred_design_questions.question: What are the concrete Rust type and API shapes for world identity, bounded region requests, readiness observation, material queries, mutation commands, streaming lifecycle, and persistence deltas?
options: Define a single public crate with a monolithic World API covering the listed surface.
Split the public surface across a small family of tightly scoped crates while preserving one consumer-facing boundary.
Leave crate packaging open and specify only traits or modules that match the listed capabilities.
deferred_design_questions.rationale: Configured sources fix the consumer-visible capability boundary and correctness properties, not the exact API packaging or type design. That is an implementation choice for later design.

deferred_design_questions.question: What machine-specific performance thresholds, if any, should gate correctness or release of the substrate?
options: Report performance with machine identity only; no numeric gate in this milestone.
Add provisional numeric targets later with an explicit machine profile.
Treat performance gates as consumer-repo concerns outside Moria.
deferred_design_questions.rationale: The program brief requires performance reporting with machine identity and explicitly declines a machine-specific correctness threshold; choosing thresholds is design or ops, not product identity.

deferred_design_questions.question: How far may the in-repo validation executable go beyond free-fly camera and diagnostics while remaining a non-game public-API harness?
options: Headless fixtures plus a minimal free-fly visual fixture only.
Free-fly visual fixture plus additional diagnostic overlays that still use only public APIs.
Any demo presentation that still refuses privileged world paths and game systems.
deferred_design_questions.rationale: Binding text forbids a game prototype, player controller, and Product One assets in Moria, but does not freeze every harness UX detail. Harness presentation details belong to design once the non-game public-API constraint is kept.
